statement: Mercia and Wessex contested hegemony over England south of the Humber from the 7th century through the Viking Age. Mercia dominated under Æthelbald (716–757) and Offa (757–796) — the latter building Offa's Dyke as a Welsh border and receiving papal recognition as a near-king. Wessex reasserted itself under Ecgberht (802–839). The Viking Great Army destroyed Mercia as an independent kingdom (877); Mercia was thereafter governed jointly by Alfred's son-in-law Æthelred and, after Æthelred's death, by Alfred's daughter Æthelflæd 'Lady of the Mercians,' who completed the Danelaw reconquest before her death (918).
